newsitem.title: USA: Former Miami, Fla., city manager faces new charges.
newsitem.headline: Former Miami, Fla., city manager faces new charges.

text.p: A federal grand jury has indicted former Miami City Manager Cesar Odio and a lobbyist on six new charges of conspiracy, embezzlement and witness tampering, prosecutors said Wednesday.

Odio and the lobbyist, Jorge Luis de Cardenas, were to be arraigned Wednesday in Miami federal court on the new charges, which carry a maximum prison sentence of 35 years and up to $1.5 million in fines.
The charges, made public late Tuesday, stem from an FBI probe of alleged public finance corruption in Miami and Dade County.
Odio and de Cardenas were charged with conspiring with former Miami city manager Manohar Surana to embezzle city funds through a contract with a health care company.
The indictment alleges that they conspired to add $12,500 a month to the city's insurance payments and divide the extra money among themselves.
The indictment also charges that Odio allegedly told Surana, a native of India, to blame his accented English for a misunderstanding that caused the confusion.

Odio and de Cardenas have been free under $100,000 bond since their arrests on Sept 11. The arrests were based on federal investigators' affidavits, which preceded the formal indictment by the grand jury.

Neither Odio nor de Cardenas were immediately available for comment Wednesday. Odio told the Miami Herald that he is innocent and that the indictment was "a fine creative writing exercise by the U.S. attorney's Office."
Prosecutors said Surana has agreed to plead guilty to unspecified charges and was cooperating with investigartors.

ormer city commissioner Miller Dawkins has already pleaded gulty to accepting $75,000 from a computer company seeking a city contract. He is free pending sentencing in January and faces up to 10 years in prison.
